notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Long white plates with the blue EU strip on the left, including the back plate. UK back plates are yellow and usually lack the strip.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Warning signs are yellow diamonds, the only ones in Europe. Regulatory signs keep the usual red border.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Yellow dashes along the road edge are very common. They are essentially never seen in the UK.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Signs are often bilingual: English in regular type and the local Celtic language in italics, including place names.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Chevrons are yellow on black, in single or multiple arrow versions. UK chevrons are white on black.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: The yield sign says YIELD; UK signs say GIVE WAY.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Yellow warning stickers on poles show a lightning bolt but no zapped figure, often with a second small outlined sticker below.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Wooden poles, often with climbing steps bolted on like thin horizontal rods and sometimes metal crossbars.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Green and white bollards are a helpful hint in a coin flip against the UK, though not unique.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Rural metal gates with rounded corners are very common; UK ones usually have square corners.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Tiny rural lanes with a grass strip down the middle are common and help split this country from the UK.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Cream-white buildings with black roofs and sometimes grey corner stones; terraced rows in cities.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Very green farmland with hedgerows lining roads and dividing fields; driving is on the left.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Double yellow lines at road sides in towns mark no parking; also seen in the UK and Malta.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Crossings are often marked by a black and white post topped with a yellow globe, same as the UK.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Regional roads have 3 digits; the first digit gives the area, numbered anticlockwise around the island from the capital.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Rugged hills and low mountains with brownish-yellow grass, moorland and exposed rock, unlike the neat eastern fields.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: A thin, unlined, very hilly rural road with Generation 4 coverage is likely in the far northwest.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Mountains south of the capital resemble the west coast ones, but they never show the sea.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Distinctive tabletop mountains in the north of Sligo and Leitrim.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: A karst area of bare grey limestone rock around the national park in the west.
